revised.summary:
I checked all 21 critique issues against the code. All 21 hold; issue 6 (the twin) is taken in part and issue 13 (the grouped commands) is fixed through cross-app-proposals' verb notation. The revised design is folded in; full text: /home/user/Stagewatch/docs/ecosystem/windows-for-peers.md. Its §9 answers each issue.

**For the operator.** On Stagewatch they grant a window to a show app: Screens → Windows → right-click → Grant to ▸ Patterns FOH, or `window grant lobby <app id>` on any transport. Nobody copies an address. The app receives the window only on its own key-verified node link.

**For Patterns** (it has a browser):
- It opens the page over pinned TLS, or over loopback when Stagewatch is on the same machine. It now dials 127.0.0.1 itself when the hello comes from this machine.
- The window appears as a Library tile, a screen tile's right-click entry, a Run strip chip, in the module, and as `SCREEN 2 WINDOW lobby`.
- That live verb works only once the page is ready. Before that it is refused and points to `SCREEN 2 PVW WINDOW lobby` then `SCREEN 2 TAKE`, so the air never goes black or white while a browser starts.
- Nothing on air ever shows words or white. A held page is drawn only while the window shell (read through an injected observer) says it has its assignment and is not gone. Every other case draws black. There is no about:blank.
- Grants survive link loss and restarts (persisted in the local `Control` section, never twinned).
- The standby twin needs its own grant. A twin word tells the main which windows the standby holds, and the Super Check names any on-air window it lacks.

**For PlayMap** (no browser):
- It draws a granted window itself as a new source kind, `window:<id>`, and reports what it drew. It never holds a token.
- The source fails closed: an unknown or withdrawn window draws black, never the followed timer. A restart draws the window's loss state before the link is back.
- Draw grants use node-link-only messages. Its old screen `identify` can no longer fire `OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL`.
- Its plain timer finally draws everything Stagewatch sends. The flash follows leader time, and query flags it does not draw are reported as an error.
- `MEDIA IMPORT` of a page, a private address or an https stream is refused with the reason.

**Secrets stay held.**
- Patterns' mount key is `stagewatch://<sw>/<window id>` or `kept://host:port/<id>`. A raw window address that reaches the model from anywhere publishes as `unkept://host:port` and is inert.
- Only Stagewatch window addresses are held automatically; other private-looking addresses only when the operator ticks Keep.
- Kept passes are the show's secrets, on Patterns' existing `Secrets` list, so the bundle masks them and the twin handles them under `SendSecrets`.
- The approved-line log is scrubbed. A fence test covers every exit door, including `InputLabels` and the twin's wire.

**Every reader sees the same chain.** Stagewatch's context, `/api/windows`, the operator frame's `windows` block, the Companion feedbacks, the copilot's facts and Patterns' Eye all read "lobby → /clock → granted to Patterns FOH → Patterns FOH says: Screen 2". Placements are accepted only from key-verified holders of the grant, and are worded as the app's claim.

**Stagewatch's own rules get tighter:**
- Every grant-address link ends black on withdraw, delete and revoke.
- A node key may ask a grant only for itself; the desk shows the proposed line, not the peer's reason.
- A key that once crossed the LAN unencrypted while TLS was offered never receives a page address.
- `WindowStatus()` keeps its one-row-per-window shape. A bounded `ViewerStatus()` sits beside it.
- The context commands use cross-app-proposals' §6 verb notation, so the desk can still rate them.

**Process changes:**
- Tombstones for dead addresses are dropped: the lockout burst was never measured. An e2e step guards the case instead.
- A maintainer decision gate (D0) on the Show Bus §1 rule 5 wording and Stagewatch's CLAUDE.md doctrine line comes before any grant path is sent.

**Spec:** Show Bus 1.3 gains §12 Windows, the caps `windows`, `pages` and `window-draw`, and the `@<node>/<item>` link end.

decisions.decision: D0: a maintainer decision gate before SW-W3. Show Bus §1 rule 5 names exactly two carriers of a pass-address: a browser's address bar, and one key-verified node link (TLS or local) to the grant's node. Stagewatch CLAUDE.md's doctrine line is the maintainer's to change.
decisions.why: Today the spec says secrets ride in no URL, and Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md:38-39 says window addresses ride in no frame. The wire must not do what the spec and doctrine forbid. No agent unit edits CLAUDE.md.
decisions.alternatives: 'Offer' the amendment after landing (the original design). That ships a contradiction.

decisions.decision: D1/D2: `window grant <window> <app>` (high risk), delivered only on the app's key-verified node link. A page grant has its own /w/<token>; a draw grant has none; at most 4 per window. revoke rotates the main and every page-grant token. Every window link whose grant token stops resolving (withdraw, delete or revoke) hears {type:window,revoked:true,black:true}.
decisions.why: Withdrawing one app stops only its address, and Stagewatch observes which viewer is the app's. Today SendLoop sends the plain WindowGone on any token miss (WebServer.cs:1248-1253,1285), so a revoke would put the 'address replaced' notice on Patterns' air.
decisions.alternatives: Hand out the main token: withdrawing it kills every TV, and the app's viewer can't be told apart. Black only on withdraw: revoke leaks the notice.

decisions.decision: D3: two ways to hold a window. how:page (Patterns, ability `pages`) and how:draw (PlayMap, ability `window-draw`). `how` is chosen at grant time from the link's can= or the hello caps; delivery always checks the current key-verified link's can=. Otherwise the grant row says `cannot` with the reason.
decisions.why: PlayMap has no browser. Hello caps are unauthenticated UDP, so they may pick `how` but never authorise delivery.
decisions.alternatives: G11's Authorization: Window header. It puts a pass in PlayMap's store and needs a second socket.

decisions.decision: D4: a page path travels only over TLS or a local link. Local means loopback or one of this machine's own interface addresses. Patterns and PlayMap dial 127.0.0.1 when the hello is this machine's. A node key seen on a plain non-local link while TLS was offered is marked clearSeen and never gets a path until it is replaced.
decisions.why: Both peers dial the hello's address (StagewatchLinkService.cs:238, StagewatchLink.cs:63-75), and the hello goes to broadcast and loopback, so 'plain loopback' rarely happened. A key sniffed in clear could otherwise be replayed over TLS to fetch the pass.
decisions.alternatives: Refuse every plain node key when TLS is offered. That is peers-not-screens' call, and it would cut AGMessage's plain link for a need only grants have.

decisions.decision: D5: Patterns' mount key is a held address (stagewatch://<sw>/<wid> or kept://host:port/<id>). The fence sits in Core at InputKeys.Web and MediaLocator: any raw Stagewatch window URL publishes as unkept://host:port with the token stripped. That form never resolves (it draws black) and a Super Check row names it. There is no show-load migration.
decisions.why: G09 leaks through the key itself (STATE, Eye, context, residency, InputLabels, Library, logs). Fixing the key fixes every reader, and the key fence makes a raw address from any source inert. Patterns' brief says no legacy is considered.
decisions.alternatives: Redact each reader (at least nine; the next would leak). Migrate at load (scope creep with no measured cause; dropped per review).

decisions.decision: D6: kept passes are the show's secrets, as WebConfig.Passes[{Id,Label,Secret}]. Secrets.Names masks `Secret` in the bundle. The twin carries them under SendSecrets (CarriesSecrets gains Web) and the standby keeps its own (OwnSecrets/KeepSecrets). Only Stagewatch window paths are held automatically; other addresses only when the operator ticks 'Keep as the show's secret'.
decisions.why: Secrets is 'the one list every exit door reads' (Secrets.cs:8-28). It covers the twin promise that the show's credentials travel. The narrower auto-rule answers the scope critique.
decisions.alternatives: A parallel per-machine webpasses.json: never twinned, so a takeover goes black, and a second store the exits don't read.

decisions.decision: D7: grants outlive the link. Patterns persists each delivered grant in Control.Stagewatch.Grants ({Sw,Window,Name,How,Base,Secret}; local section, masked). PlayMap persists HeldWindows (no secret) in NodeSettings. Only a received grants list that omits a window removes it. rev is per link.
decisions.why: Clearing on disconnect would blank granted windows on every Stagewatch restart or link blip. Persisting lets a restart resolve at once, and the shell's own onLoss rule covers an outage.
decisions.alternatives: Hold grants in memory only: black after every restart until TLS, auth and grants complete.

decisions.decision: D8: no about:blank. For a held Stagewatch page, Patterns injects a document-created observer that posts SWShell.state() to the host. The source is Withheld (drawn black) unless navigation succeeded, rev>0 and link≠gone. Every held branch draws black: no page, a DrawInput failure (no PlaceholderCard) and a layer's status words.
decisions.why: WebView2 has no DefaultBackgroundColor set, so about:blank captures white. MediaAndParticlePatterns.cs:152-155 and LayerRenderer.cs:143-155 put words on air. SWShell.state() and the data-* attributes exist since 2.17, so this works without a Stagewatch change.
decisions.alternatives: A black data: page (still races the old frames). Polling ExecuteScriptAsync (slower; the notice could be captured between polls).

decisions.decision: D9: SCREEN n WINDOW is live only when the page is ready (mounted, not Withheld, loading empty, link ok). Otherwise it is refused, with nothing changed, and steered to SCREEN n PVW WINDOW then SCREEN n TAKE. SCREEN n TAKE of a staged held page that isn't ready is refused too.
decisions.why: One air: a live verb never blanks a screen, and AirState never disagrees with the glass. SCREEN n TAKE already exists (ControlProtocol.cs:477-478).
decisions.alternatives: Keep the previous picture until ready. AirState would then say the window while the glass shows the old picture.

decisions.decision: D10: placement is the app's claim, posted as a §6 link end `@<node>/<item>`. Stagewatch takes it only from a key-verified context whose node holds a grant of that window with an open or shown viewer, and words it 'Patterns FOH says: Screen 2'.
decisions.why: PeerContexts.Accept stores any valid context (ShowBus.cs:57-69), so otherwise any node could make Stagewatch claim where a window is shown.
decisions.alternatives: A private 'placed' message: no Eye or AI would read it. Trusting every context: forgeable.

decisions.decision: D11: G23. timer -feeds-> window only while the window shows a page; no link for health items. 13 command rows in cross-app-proposals' §6 notation (A|B words, ' | ' forms, […], …), rated by its VerbSyntax; SW-W1 depends on that unit. Patterns' brief cap goes 12→32.
decisions.why: Today's RiskFromCommands (Approvals.cs:225-237) can't match grouped rows ('show|cue' ≠ 'show'). cross-app-proposals already defines and builds the notation. Patterns has no matcher of its own.
decisions.alternatives: One plain template per row (the fallback if VerbSyntax slips): about 30 rows, all needing the raised cap.

decisions.decision: D12: placement on Patterns is Patterns' act (SCREEN n WINDOW, PVW WINDOW, NODES ASK WINDOW). Proposal fence: in ProposalDesk.Submit, a node-key proposal whose line is `window grant …` must name its own from.id, or it gets 'a show app may ask a window only for itself'. The desk shows the line, never the peer's reason, as the headline for window grants.
decisions.why: Submit binds only from.id (Approvals.cs:92), and the desk's headline is the peer's reason (MainViewModel.Desk.cs:99). A node could otherwise ask a grant for another node behind a misleading reason.

decisions.decision: D13: draw grants ride node-link-only types (window-assign, window-end, window-identify; window-shown back). window reload is refused for a window only apps draw. peers-not-screens §2.1 gains 'the only window messages a node link hears are §12's, for its own grants'.
decisions.why: PlayMap turns a link `identify` into OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL 5 (NetworkHost.cs:782-783). ReloadWindows reaches only sockets, so a reload receipt would claim work that never happened.
decisions.alternatives: Reuse window/identify types: either destructive on air or silently dropped.

decisions.decision: D14: PlayMap's window source is a new SourceKind.Window (`window:<id>`, a Spine: commit). It always yields a frame: black if unknown or ended, the onLoss state while the link is down. It never falls back to the followed timer. The flash phase is a function of leader time; both pictures are pre-drawn. Unhonoured query flags are reported in error.
decisions.why: timer:<id> ignores its id (EngineSources.cs:178-179), and a null lease keeps the last picture (SourceResolver.cs:417-432), so a fallback fails open to a live countdown. Mapper's doctrine: content = f(leader time).
decisions.alternatives: A window-shaped id inside timer: (ambiguous, still the Timer kind's fallback). Black via a null lease (keeps the stale picture).

decisions.decision: D15: no tombstones. The papers say 'no measurement this round', and e2e step 6 (revoke, reload, then a real window from the same address) guards the lockout.
decisions.why: A dead token draws one WindowGone and the shell stops (WebServer.cs:1179-1189, window.js:250), and Patterns never reloads (WebFrameSource.cs:272). There is no measured cause, and both CLAUDE.md files require one before a governor lands.
decisions.alternatives: Land tombstones anyway: a governor without a measured cause.

decisions.decision: D16: the twin. A grant belongs to a node, and a standby is a node with its own id (ServiceKernel.cs:181). Grant paths never ride the plain-TCP twin link (OPEN L36). A twin word WINDOWS (standby → main, ids only) feeds a Super Check row naming on-air windows the standby lacks. Kept passes travel as show credentials (D6). DRILL scenario 23.
decisions.why: Carrying grant paths would send a pass across the LAN in clear, which D4 forbids. Telling the operator before the show is fail-safe.
decisions.alternatives: Carry the main's grant paths on the twin (the critique's fix): a readable pass on plain TCP.

decisions.decision: D17: WindowStatus() keeps one row per window (plus an appended Drawn). A new ViewerStatus() gives one row per (window, via), bounded at (MaxGrants+1)×Max = 320 and evicted per key, never cleared whole.
decisions.why: Several readers key by window id: ToDictionary at WebServer.cs:680, FirstOrDefault at ScreenWindows.cs:330, the Screens subtitle and the tests' .Single. A whole clear at 4×Max (:1392) would flicker lights.
decisions.alternatives: Change WindowStatus to per-via rows: /api/windows throws on a window's second viewer.

decisions.decision: D18: G46 left: a window shows only its own Stagewatch's pages.
decisions.why: No peer serves a frameable page, and a cross-origin page breaks the window's CSP, its window.SW check and pinning.
decisions.alternatives: A Stagewatch page drawing peers' contexts (in WHATS_NEXT; no measured ask).

revised.wire:
STAGEWATCH — one grammar on HTTP /api/window/…, WS {cmd:"window",args}, OSC /stagewatch/window, Companion WINDOW …, MCP run_command and the copilot.

**Commands** (both high risk in Copilot.Classify)
- `window grant <window> <app>`
  - One window, never `all`.
  - app is a Show Bus id `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}`, or a quoted name when it is unique.
- `window withdraw <window|all> [<app>]`
  - The window, or `all`, must be named. A bare `window withdraw` is refused: "window withdraw takes a window (or all)".

**Receipt**
```
{"type":"receipt","id":"a1","ok":true,"stage":"applied","effect":"lobby granted to Patterns FOH (9f8e7d6c) as a page — it takes the address when it links with its node key","refs":{"window":"wk3m9x2","node":"9f8e7d6c"}}
```
When `how` came from hello caps, the effect adds "(it says it shows pages; checked when it links)".

**Refusals** (ok:false, nothing changed)
- `No show app called "x" on the show network (heard: …)`
- `"FOH" names 2 show apps — use its id (…)`
- `<app> can't show a window: it offers neither pages nor window-draw`
- `lobby is already granted to <app>`
- `lobby is granted to 4 show apps already — withdraw one first`
- `Grant one window at a time`
- `lobby isn't granted to anyone`
- For reload: `lobby is drawn by <app>, which has no page to reload — window show lobby <page> sends it again`

**Settings** (`remote.windows[]`, appended)
```
"grants":[{"node","t","name","how":"page"|"draw","token":"<26>"|"","made":"<ISO>"}]
```
- At most 4 per window.
- A draw grant's token is "".
- `remote.apiKeys[]` gains `"clearSeen":"<ISO>"|""`, appended.

**Node link** (peers-not-screens: `/ws?node=<id>&t=<kind>`, `Authorization: Bearer <node key>`)
- Adds `&can=pages,window-draw`: at most 4 words of `[a-z-]{1,16}`; unknown words are ignored.

Stagewatch → app. Sent only on links with verified:"key" bound to the grant's node, after `auth` and before any frame, then whole on every byte change:
```
{"type":"grants","from":"<sw id>","rev":<int>,"link":"tls"|"local"|"plain","grants":[{"window":"wk3m9x2","name":"lobby","how":"page"|"draw","path":"/w/<26>"|"","cannot":"<words>"|""}]}
```
- `path` is non-empty only when all of these hold:
  - how=page;
  - this link's can has `pages`;
  - link is tls or local (loopback, or one of Stagewatch's own interface addresses);
  - the key is not clearSeen.
- `cannot` is one of:
  - `this link is not encrypted — link over wss://`
  - `this node's key crossed the network unencrypted — the Stagewatch operator makes it a new key`
  - `this link doesn't offer pages`
  - `this link doesn't offer window-draw`
- `rev` is per process. The receiver takes the first grants on each new link whatever its rev, and later ones only when higher.

Draw grants only, when can has window-draw:
```
{"type":"window-assign","window","name","content","hold","holdText","holdImage","onLoss","fadeMs","rev"}
{"type":"window-end","window","why":"withdrawn"|"deleted"}
{"type":"window-identify","window","name"}
```

App → Stagewatch:
```
{"type":"grants-seen","rev":<int>,"cannot":""|"<≤200 chars>"}
{"type":"window-shown","window","rev","content","hold","ms","error"}
```
`window-shown` is accepted only for a draw grant of that window held by this link's node. Otherwise:
```
{"type":"error","error":"only a show app a window is granted to draw may say what it draws"}
```
A node link never hears window, identify, reload, redirect or disconnect (an amendment to peers-not-screens §2.1).

**Window link on a grant address**
- `/ws?win=<grant token>&detail=1`, unchanged.
- When a grant token stops resolving (withdraw, delete or revoke), it hears `{"type":"window","revoked":true,"black":true}`. The shell draws plain black (no #gone text), sets `data-link="gone"` and stops.
- The main address keeps today's message.

**GET /api/windows** (read), per window, appended:
```
"drawn":<int>,"grants":[{"node","t","name","how","linked","link","delivered","open","state","words"}]
```
- `state` is one of `waiting`, `plain`, `key-in-clear`, `cannot`, `sent`, `held`, `open`, `shown` or `stale`.
- A grant path is never listed, for any credential.
- connected, shown, inStep and device are unchanged; they come from the aggregate row.

**Context §6**
- Window items' words add grants and claims ("Patterns FOH says: Screen 2 — LED wall"). The light is the worst over opened viewers.
- Links: `{"from":"timer","to":"window:<name>","kind":"feeds"}` only while it shows a page; none for health items.
- Commands: 13 rows in the §6 notation (cross-app-proposals' VerbSyntax):
  1. `note <text>` — low
  2. `message <text> [warning]` — review
  3. `signal standby <dept> <cue>` — review
  4. `signal go <dept> <cue> | signal go all` — high
  5. `nudge|trim|delay …` — review
  6. `next | start | pause` — high
  7. `blackout` — high
  8. `window show|cue <window> <page or setup or holding or black>` — high
  9. `window hold|release <window or all>` — high
  10. `window grant <window> <app> | window withdraw <window or all> [<app>]` — high
  11. `window identify|reload|revoke|delete <window>` — high
  12. `window new|rename|loss|fade <window> …` — low
  13. `patterns end|restart|play|pause|stop|seek …` — high
- Peer contexts: `links` are read (≤400, ends ≤120); the items cap is 200.

**Detail frame** (operator only), last block after rooms:
```
"windows":[{"name","light","inStep","hold","showing","granted","on"}]
```
- Never a token.
- The public frames carry none.

**Proposals** (ProposalDesk.Submit): with a node key, a line `window grant <w> <app>` must have app == from.id. Otherwise `a show app may ask a window only for itself`.

**Hello caps**
- Stagewatch: `windows`.
- Patterns: `pages`.
- PlayMap: `window-draw`.

**SHOWBUS 1.3**
- §1 rule 5: the exemption names two carriers: the browser's address bar, and one key-verified node link (TLS or local) to the grant's node.
- §2: the caps.
- §6: link end `@<node id>/<item id>`, one hop. Another node's item as `from` is that node's claim.
- §12 Windows: grants and these messages, the per-link rev, the path rule, the black end, held forms, placement claims, and "a host reads SWShell.state()/data-* and draws black, never words, until it can".

PATTERNS — TCP 9697 / HTTP /api/cmd, paired as today.

**Verbs**
- `SCREEN <n> WINDOW <window>` — live, own picture, only when ready:
  ```
  OK "Stagewatch lobby on Screen 2 alone — every other screen stays."
  ```
- `SCREEN <n> PVW WINDOW <window>` and `PVW WINDOW <window>` — staged; they open the page.
- `NODES ASK WINDOW <window>`:
  ```
  OK "asked Stagewatch Hall A for window lobby (pending there)"
  ```

**Refusals**
- `No Stagewatch window 'x' is granted to this desk (granted: …) — ask for it: NODES ASK WINDOW x`
- `Screen 2 already shows Stagewatch lobby`
- `Stagewatch lobby isn't open here yet — SCREEN 2 PVW WINDOW lobby opens it on the preview, then SCREEN 2 TAKE`
- For SCREEN n TAKE: `Stagewatch lobby is still opening on Screen 2's PVW — take it when the tile says ready`
- `Stagewatch Hall A granted lobby, but over this link it sends no address: <cannot>`
- `Web pages need Windows with the WebView2 runtime`

**ASK body** (POST /api/proposals, node key):
```
{"from":{"t":"patterns","id","name"},"target":{"t":"main","id":"<sw id>"},"line":"window grant <window> <self id>","reason":"…","risk":"high"}
```

**STATE**
- `web.url` = `stagewatch://<sw>/<wid>` | `kept://host:port/<id>` | `unkept://host:port`. Never a private URL.
- `web.page` = `"Stagewatch lobby"`.
- The residency key is the held key.
- `bus.stagewatch` gains, last:
  ```
  "windows":[{"id","name","address","state":"held|opening|ready|shown|black|cannot","screens":["2"],"words"}]
  ```

**Context**
- Link:
  ```
  {"from":"@<sw id>/window:lobby","to":"source:web:stagewatch://<sw>/<wid>","kind":"feeds"}
  ```
- Commands: `SCREEN <n> WINDOW <window>` (high), `SCREEN <n> PVW WINDOW <window>` (review), `NODES ASK WINDOW <window>` (low).

**Module**
- Action `screen_window`.
- A stage-then-take preset.
- Variable `stagewatch_windows`.

**Twin word** `WINDOWS` (standby → main): `{"held":["wk3m9x2"]}`. Ids only.

**Show model**
- `WebConfig.Passes[{Id,Label,Secret}]` (≤64).
- `StagewatchLinkConfig.Grants[{Sw,Window,Name,How,Base,Secret}]` (≤64, local Control section).
- Both are masked by `Secrets`. Passes travel on the twin under SendSecrets.

PLAYMAP (after round 3)

**Source**
- `window:<window id>` (new `SourceKind.Window`, spine).
- OUTPUT SOURCE and SURFACE SOURCE take it; there is no new verb.
- `timer:stagewatch` is unchanged.

**STATE `links.stagewatch.windows`** (new block, with fixture and card):
```
[{"id","name","sw","content","rev","shownRev","drawing":"timer|clock|holding|black|loss","on":["out1"],"error","link":"up|down"}]
```

**STATE `links.stagewatch.timer`** gains, at the end: next, urgency, flash, flashTimer, blackout, holding, holdingName, holdingFill, watermark, timeOfDay, show{}.

**MEDIA IMPORT refusals** (no item added; a private address is never echoed)
- A page or embed: `ERR pages and embeds need a browser source, which PlayMap has not built (ROADMAP L10) — send it as NDI from a browser, or have Stagewatch grant a window to this node`
- A window address: `ERR that is a Stagewatch window's private address — PlayMap draws Stagewatch windows when one is granted to this node (Stagewatch: window grant <window> <this node id>)`
- An https .m3u8 or .mpd: `ERR this node's FFmpeg is not known to open https streams — use rtsp://, srt:// or NDI`

**Context**: `@<sw id>/window:<name> -feeds-> <the output or surface drawing it>`.

issues.issue: After a withdraw, a held page that can no longer be resolved goes WHITE on air, not black. The design sends the WebView2 to about:blank and makes the pattern draw black only when `page is null`. Patterns never sets DefaultBackgroundColor, so about:blank captures as a white frame, and the mounted source still delivers it. The second PlaceholderCard, used when DrawInput fails, still puts `page.StatusText` words on the output. Both break the design's own decision 7.
issues.evidence: Patterns/src/Patterns.Rendering/Patterns/MediaAndParticlePatterns.cs:139-155 (black only for page==null; second card at DrawInput failure); grep of Patterns/src finds no DefaultBackgroundColor; WebFrameSource.cs:1389-1404 (NavigateCore); design §3 WebFrameSource 'navigates to about:blank'
issues.fix: Do not navigate to about:blank. Mark the source unresolved so the pattern draws black, or navigate to a black data: page with DefaultBackgroundColor set to black. Make every held-page failure branch, the DrawInput one included, draw black with no words. Add a Rendering test that the unresolved and the withdrawn cases are both all black.

issues.issue: PlayMap's `timer:<id>` fails open. Any id that is not a granted window, or not granted yet, falls back to the followed live timer. So after a PlayMap restart before the grants arrive, after a withdraw, or with the grant list not yet delivered, an output meant to show holding or black shows a live countdown. This is the 'stale or wrong clock in front of the room' the design forbids (decision 7).
issues.evidence: design §2.11 ('timer:stagewatch (and any id that is not a granted window) is the followed timer'); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Rendering/EngineSources.cs:178-179 (one _timer, id ignored)
issues.fix: Use a distinct source kind or prefix (`window:<id>`), or treat any id shaped like a window id (w + 6 of the window alphabet) as a window. When the window is unknown or withdrawn, draw black or its onLoss state and never the followed timer. Test the restart-before-grants and withdraw cases.

issues.issue: The draw-grant messages `identify` (and `reload` by extension) collide with existing semantics. peers-not-screens §2.1 says a node link never receives identify, reload or disconnect. Today PlayMap turns a link `identify` into `OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL 5` on every output, on-air ones included, and after PM-1 into a journal row only, so a window identify would be either destructive or silently dropped. `window reload` on a draw-only window would be counted reachable through WindowStatus, but ReloadWindows pushes only to window sockets, so the receipt claims 'Reloading lobby' while nothing happens.
issues.evidence: peers-not-screens.md:181; Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:395-407 (identify → ScreenCommand); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:782-783 (OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL 5); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WindowDirector.cs:51-55; WebServer.cs:172-186
issues.fix: Use node-link-only types (`window-identify`, carrying the window id) that no screen handler reads. Refuse `window reload` for draw grants with the reason (or define a re-draw). Amend peers-not-screens §2.1 to name these as the only window messages a node link hears.

issues.issue: Revoking a granted window puts Stagewatch's 'address replaced' notice on Patterns' air. The design sends revoked+black only when a grant ends (withdraw or delete). On `revoke`, every grant token rotates, so SendLoop's ByToken check fails and the link gets the plain WindowGone, which shows the notice. The old grant tokens are not tombstoned either, so a reload of the shell or its inner fetches counts toward the lockout.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1248-1253,1285 (WindowGone on any token miss); wwwroot/window.js:250,268-278 (revoked shows #gone); design §2.4 ('When the grant ends (withdraw or delete)'), decision 2 (revoke rotates grant tokens)
issues.fix: Any link whose Via is a grant gets {revoked:true,black:true} whenever its token stops resolving, revoke included. Tombstone rotated grant tokens like withdrawn ones. Say in REMOTE that on revoke the Patterns screen shows black, then the new shell's holding page, for about a second.

issues.issue: Changing WindowStatus() to one row per (window, via) breaks the readers that exist today. HandleWindowListAsync builds `ToDictionary(o => o.WindowId)`, which throws on the first window with two viewers, so /api/windows fails. The Screens subtitle counts viewers as 'open windows', and the row shows an arbitrary via's device. `_windowSeen` is cleared whole when it passes 4×Max = 256 entries; with up to 5 vias × 64 windows that clear keeps firing, so every light flickers back to grey.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:680 (ToDictionary), :1392 (clear at 4*Max); src/Timer.App/ScreensWindow.xaml.cs:101-116; src/Timer.Core/ScreenWindows.cs:330 (FirstOrDefault by WindowId); tests/Stagewatch.Tests/WindowTests.cs:260-267 (.Single by WindowId)
issues.fix: Keep WindowStatus() as one row per window (the aggregate) and add a separate ViewerStatus() per (window, via). Size the bound to (MaxGrants+1)×Max and evict per key instead of clearing. List every caller in SW-W3.

issues.issue: The Patterns twin/takeover chain is missing. Kept passes are 'never twinned' and grants are per node id and held in memory, so on TAKE OVER the standby holds `stagewatch://` and `kept://` keys it cannot resolve, and every granted or pasted window goes black on air. This contradicts the twin promise ('puts what the main had on air back on') and its rule that the show's credentials travel by default. The design also builds a parallel secret store instead of using `Secrets`, 'the one list every exit door reads'.
issues.evidence: Patterns/README.md:362-368,400-403; Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/Twin.cs:364-383 (WireJson sendSecrets); Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/Secrets.cs:17-28; design §6 Left ('standby twin … proposed, not designed')
issues.fix: Carry the kept passes, and the main's currently delivered grant paths, on the authenticated twin link as show credentials (honouring sendSecrets). Register them in Secrets.Names/Placed so Redact and Blank cover them at every exit. Add the takeover case to PrivateAddressFenceTests and a DRILL/QUALIFICATION row.

issues.issue: What happens to grants on link loss or restart is unspecified. Grants live in memory from the link. If Patterns clears them when the link drops, every Stagewatch restart or link blip blanks the granted windows on air, though the window shell would itself have shown its holding page. After a Patterns watchdog restart, the recovery record puts the held page back, but it stays black until TLS dial, auth and grants complete, and indefinitely if Stagewatch is down. PlayMap has the same gap before its first grants.
issues.evidence: design §3 StagewatchLinkService (SetGrants from `grants` only); decision 7 (unresolved = black); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/wwwroot/window.js:8-10,173 (shell's own link-loss holding page)
issues.fix: Grants survive link loss: only a received list without the window removes it. Persist the last delivered grant (window id → path, per Stagewatch id) in the per-machine kept store, so a restart resolves at once and the shell's own onLoss behaviour covers a Stagewatch outage. Test both.

issues.issue: `SCREEN n WINDOW` is a live take onto the air. Under decision 7 the screen draws black until the WebView2 has started and the shell has drawn, which can take seconds when a new browser of the 4 is spun up. A live verb that blanks a screen goes against 'every selection change is instant' and the air/preview doctrine.
issues.evidence: design §2.10 (live: air and edit), decision 7; Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/ShowActions.Content.cs:168-188 (SCREEN n PATTERN precedent, no media mount); Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/WebEngine.cs:24 (4 pages)
issues.fix: Keep the screen's previous picture until the held page has delivered its first frame, which the window shell signals by leaving its holding page. Otherwise, refuse the live verb while the page is not mounted, with the reason, and steer to `SCREEN n PVW WINDOW` (pre-roll) plus a take. Visibility and Effect should report 'loading' rather than Done.

issues.issue: Placement claims are taken as observed facts from any peer. WindowPlacements.From reads `@<sw>/window:<name>` links from every posted context, including unverified ones (peers-not-screens decision 8) and nodes that hold no grant of that window. Any node can make Stagewatch's context, frame and Companion feedback say 'lobby on X: Screen 2'.
issues.evidence: design §3 ShowBus.cs WindowPlacements.From(entries, ownId); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ShowBus.cs:56-69 (Accept stores any valid context); peers-not-screens.md decision 8
issues.fix: Accept a placement only from a key-verified context whose node holds a grant of that window and has an open or shown viewer for it. Word placements as the app's claim ('Patterns FOH says: Screen 2'). Test that a non-holder's link is ignored.

issues.issue: With `NODES ASK WINDOW`, a peer can ask on behalf of another node. Submit binds only `from.id` to the key. The line `window grant <window> <app>` is peer-authored, and Stagewatch's approval list shows the peer's `reason` as the request headline. A node can therefore post `window grant lobby <other id>` with the reason 'Patterns FOH asks to show window lobby'.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/Approvals.cs:91 (BindKey(from.Id) only); Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Desk.cs:99 (Request = p.Reason); design §2.10 ASK body
issues.fix: At Submit (or RiskFor), refuse a proposal from a node key whose line is `window grant` naming an app other than from.id, with words. Show the line, not the reason, as the headline for window grants. Add a ShowBusTests case.

issues.issue: The spec and the doctrine contradict the wire. The new §1 rule 5 exemption says a window address 'may be a browser's address' only, yet the `grants` message carries the path on a node link. Stagewatch CLAUDE.md says window addresses ride in no frame, and the design only 'offers' the amendment to the maintainer, while SW-W3 depends on it.
issues.evidence: design §2.9 (rule 5 wording), processNotes ('offered to the maintainer, not part of these units'); Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md:38-39
issues.fix: Word the exemption to name the second carrier explicitly: one key-verified node link, TLS or loopback, to the grant's node only. Make the doctrine line a maintainer decision gate before SW-W3, recorded in REMOTE and WHATS_NEXT, not an afterthought.

issues.issue: The TLS-or-loopback gate does not match how the peers dial. Patterns auto-dials the address the hello came from (`peer.Address`), and Stagewatch's hello goes to both broadcast and loopback, so on one laptop the address is often the LAN IP. 'One laptop over plain loopback' then rarely happens, and the path takes the unproven WebView2 certificate route. The gate also ignores a node key that has already crossed a plain link: a sniffer can replay it over TLS and receive the path.
issues.evidence: Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/StagewatchLinkService.cs:238 (dials peer.Address); Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:27-28 (hello to broadcast and loopback); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:325 (IsLoopback on the remote address)
issues.fix: Have Patterns and PlayMap dial 127.0.0.1 when the hello's host is this machine. Have Stagewatch treat its own interface addresses as local. Alternatively refuse node keys on plain non-loopback links when TLS is offered, so a key never crosses in the clear.

issues.issue: The 13 grouped command rows ('window show|cue <window> …', 'next | start | pause', 'nudge|trim|delay …') are no longer verb templates. ProposalDesk.RiskFromCommands matches fixed words up to the first placeholder, and §11 says the desk takes risk from the target's listed verbs. 'next | start | pause' needs 5 words to match, and 'show|cue' never equals 'show'. The rows stop being machine-readable risk entries for any reader.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/Approvals.cs:224-236 (RiskFromCommands); Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:197-198 (§11 risk from commands); design §2.6
issues.fix: Keep one matchable template per row, and raise Patterns' brief cap instead. Or define an alternation syntax in §6 and teach RiskFromCommands (and Patterns' matcher) to expand it, with tests.

issues.issue: The kept-pass rule is scope creep with real regressions. Any URL carrying a query word such as key, token or apikey is moved into a machine-local file and migrated at show load. Third-party pages (signage, dashboards, sheets) then go black on any other machine and on the twin. G09 concerns /w/ window paths, and Patterns' brief says no legacy is considered, which argues against migrating old shows.
issues.evidence: design decision 6; gaps.json G09 (fix scoped to /w/ paths); Patterns/CLAUDE.md standing brief ('No legacy or previous version is considered')
issues.fix: Hold only Stagewatch window paths automatically. Offer 'keep this address on this machine' for other private-looking URLs as an operator choice. Drop the show-load migration, or justify it by measurement.

issues.issue: The tombstones are presented as having a 'measured cause', but nothing was measured. After `revoked()` the shell stops, and Patterns has no automatic reload, so the burst of 404s is hypothetical. Both CLAUDE.md files say no governor lands without a measured cause. A successful key request from the same IP also already clears the failure count.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/wwwroot/window.js:268-278 (stops); Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/WebFrameSource.cs:272 (ProcessFailed only sets words; no auto-reload); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1083 (TryRemove on key success)
issues.fix: First reproduce the lockout without tombstones in the rig e2e, for example on revoke with a reload, and land tombstones only if it occurs. Otherwise write 'no measurement this round' and drop them.

issues.issue: `how` is fixed at grant time, possibly from hello caps (unauthenticated UDP), and the path is then sent on every later link whatever that link's `can=` offers now.
issues.evidence: design decision 3 ('else from hello caps'), §2.3

issues.issue: The PlayMap native subset reports `shown` with content it did not honour, such as `/clock?h=12` or `/viewer?…` flags, which turns the window green. The flash phase is specified on an injected local clock, though Mapper's doctrine is frame = f(leader time).
issues.evidence: design §3 NativeWindows.Classify; Mapper/CLAUDE.md doctrine ('Content is a pure function of show time')
issues.fix: Report `error` (amber) for query flags that are not honoured. Derive the flash phase from leader time at vblank.
